title: Time-sliced priority scheduler with QoS buckets for prefill/decode
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Summary: Implement a time-sliced priority scheduler that partitions prefill and decode work into configurable QoS buckets (realtime, interactive, best-effort) and enforces time-slices per bucket with deadline-aware arbitration. This aims to improve tail latency for latency-sensitive traffic while preserving throughput for background workloads.

Goals:
- Reduce 99th percentile end-to-end latency for interactive prefill/decode by 25% under mixed loads.
- Ensure best-effort workloads continue to achieve >60% baseline throughput under bursty realtime traffic.
- Provide deterministic knobs (bucket capacities, slice length, admission thresholds) for Dedicated customers to tune latency vs cost.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change per-model kernel selection heuristics or quantization profiles (those are separate).
- Not implementing a full per-token fairness auction; focus is on time-sliced enforcement and priority ceilings.

Design overview:
- Work is classified at ingress into QoS buckets based on request metadata (route, priority header, customer SLA).
- Scheduler cycles through buckets in configurable order, granting each a time-slice (ms) on the GPU compute worker. Within a slice, prefills and decodes are admitted up to a work cap.
- Deadlines: requests carry soft-deadline = now + route_slo. If deadline within next slice, they are promoted to the next higher bucket (promotion is bounded to avoid starvation).
- Fairness: maintain a sliding deficit counter per bucket to ensure long-term proportional share; best-effort receives background fill when realtime/interactive queues are empty.
- Phase-splitting: distinguish prefill vs decode phases and allow different slice ratios (e.g., 70% decode time for interactive, 30% prefill).
- Eviction and KV cache considerations: when a prefill is evicted due to slice expiry, ensure KV cache is preserved for prioritized sessions; evicted prefill work reports partial progress to caller to enable retries without duplicating full prefill when resumed.

Metrics and observability:
- New counters and histograms: bucket_admissions, bucket_rejections, slice_utilization_ms, per-bucket_p99_latency, per-bucket_throughput_tps, prefill_evictions.
- Dashboards: mixed-workload SLO dashboard comparing baseline vs feature branch (link in links).

Experiment plan:
1) Local simulation harness: reproduce mixed workload (40% interactive short-decoder, 40% realtime long-stream, 20% background batches). Iterate on slice sizes.
2) Small canary: deploy to a dedicated pool for internal customers. Monitor p50/p95/p99 and throughput regressions for best-effort.
3) Gradual rollout with opt-in per-customer flag; gate by successful canary metrics.

Trade-offs considered:
- Time-slicing vs weighted-round-robin: slices prioritize latency isolation but can underutilize small slices if workload granularity mismatches; we'll include adaptive slice coalescing.
- Strict deadlines vs promotion: aggressive promotion reduces latency but risks starving background jobs; we implement promotion caps and deficit accounting.
- Prefill eviction cost: resuming prefill work has overhead; to mitigate, we plan to snapshot prefill progress at slice boundaries for common models.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Ingress tagging and QoS bucket mapping (ENG).
- Scheduler core: time-slice loop, promotion logic, deficit counters (ENG).
- Prefill checkpointing hooks and eviction reporting (runtime + worker) (ENG).
- Metrics and dashboarding (Observability) (ENG).
- E2E simulation harness + workload generator (QA/Eng).

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary shows >=25% p99 reduction for interactive bucket under defined mixed load without causing >15% throughput regression for best-effort.
- Metrics and dashboards populated and alerting thresholds configured.
- Feature flag to disable scheduling policy per pool.
- Design doc and PRs reviewed and merged.
